title: Spend Round Trips, Not Calls
tagline: Batching is part of the tool signature, because a request in a prompt is one a model can stop honouring.

story.problem: A traced scout run spent 166 of its 220 seconds deciding what to call next and 27 running the tools, with the remainder unattributed in the source. The provider is not what the couple waits for — the model's turn is, and there is one of those for every tool call it decides to make. Worse, a tool-calling transcript re-sends every prior turn, so each extra round trip re-reads a transcript that has grown since the last one, and a result returned twice is re-billed on every later model call. The scout instructions had asked for batched searches before web_search could accept one, which made batching a request the model could quietly stop honouring.
story.solution: Move batching into the tool signature: agent/tools/web_search.ts takes queries as an array capped at four, runs them through one Promise.all, and returns results grouped by query. Both queries and query stay optional so neither shape can be a schema failure — an unsatisfiable schema kills a subagent session outright — and an empty batch returns status no_query instead of throwing. filterSeen in agent/lib/search-budget.ts suppresses URLs the session has already been shown, across the whole batch rather than per query, bounded to the last 400. The scout's todo tool is disabled because it spent two round trips on bookkeeping the search budget already bounds, and the same batching argument is applied one level up: the planner dispatches every scout in a single response.
story.outcome: One committed RunResult, runs/eve-boston-boho.json, shows five specialists taking 23, 15, 14, 15 and 12 steps against 6, 4, 4, 2 and 4 web_search calls — 20 search calls across 79 steps. The concurrent fan-out puts 335.8s of specialist time inside a 114.0s run, with the slowest specialist at 75.5s and the planner parked for 102,781ms of its own. Nothing here is gated on a latency figure: wall clock is measured and published, never asserted. record_vendor is deliberately left unbatched, because a finding that does not survive a truncation is worse than a slow one.

prerequisites: An eve install with declared subagents and defineState (^0.24.4)
TAVILY_API_KEY for live search and NEBIUS_API_KEY for the model — the command in the recipe needs neither
Recipe 05 (Governance): the per-session query counter this tool reserves against before it dials out
More than one traced run, if you want to know whether a change moved anything

quickstart.clone: git clone https://github.com/jaredwerba/vendor-scout.git && cd vendor-scout && npm install
quickstart.configure: Nothing to configure to read the committed run artifact. To regenerate it against the live deployment, put NEBIUS_API_KEY and TAVILY_API_KEY in .env.local (full list in README.md) and run npm run run:eve -- boston-boho.
